mainTopic: רב's rulings following רבי מאיר's principle (ערך כלי, a friend's animal), and the מחלוקת over whether a נכרי can be מעריך or נערך
overview: The amud opens by explaining why רב had to say that one who pledges 'ערך כלי עלי' pays the כלי's value. His ruling shows that רבי מאיר's reason is 'a person does not say words for nothing,' and not a גזירה. The גמרא then brings רב's ruling that one who consecrates his friend's animal pays its value. This also follows רבי מאיר. Both rulings are needed, because an animal can really become holy, so we might have thought he meant to make the animal itself holy. רב אשי limits this ruling to when the person said 'עלי' (upon me), not 'הרי זו' (this is holy). A new משנה follows: רבי מאיר says a נכרי can be valued but cannot make an ערך vow, and רבי יהודה says the opposite. Each one reads the words 'בני ישראל' and 'איש' his own way. רבא says רבי מאיר's ruling makes sense because of the פסוק in עזרא, 'לא לכם ולנו', while רבי יהודה's proof is the better one. The גמרא then asks how רבי יהודה reads that פסוק. רב חסדא's answer, that the money is put away, is challenged from the laws of מעילה. רבא answers instead that the refusal in עזרא was only because those people were trying to weaken the builders.

steps.title: Why did רב need to say his ruling according to רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: If רב's ruling about ערך כלי simply follows רבי מאיר, what does it add?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי מאיר, why was רב's ruling needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב bothered to say that one who pledges 'ערך כלי' pays its value. רבי מאיר already says the same kind of thing about a baby less than a month old.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that רב's ruling matches רבי מאיר. If רבי מאיר already makes a person pay value when there is no ערך, רב's statement seems to add nothing. The גמרא wants to know what new point רב is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Why was it needed? (What does this statement add?)
The fixed amount the תורה sets for a person, based on age and gender

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Meir,
why was it necessary?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי מֵאִיר לְמַאי אִיצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the earlier identification of רב's ruling with רבי מאיר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point does רב's ruling teach beyond רבי מאיר's known position?

steps.title: רב shows that רבי מאיר's reason is not a decree
steps.stepSummary: Without רב, we might think רבי מאיר's ruling was only a גזירה about babies. רב teaches that the real reason is that people do not speak for nothing, and that applies to a כלי too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי מאיר's reason there is a decree: he makes one pay for a baby less than a month old because of a baby who is a month old. Here, with a כלי, there is nothing to decree about, so he would not make one pay. רב teaches us that רבי מאיר's reason is that a person does not say words for nothing. So there is no difference between the two cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב's ruling adds. It tells us why רבי מאיר makes a person pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible reasons for רבי מאיר. One is a גזירה: a baby under a month might be confused with a one-month-old, who does have a ערך. The other is that a person's words must mean something. A כלי can't be confused with a baby, so only the second reason would apply to it. רב's ruling proves that the second reason is the right one.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken thought the statement comes to rule out)
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Because of (a concern about a similar case)
It teaches us (the new point)
A person does not say his words for nothing
Less than a month old (a baby with no ערך)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's reason is 'אין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה'. So it applies to any pledge of ערך where there is no ערך, whether a young baby or a כלי.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once the reason is about the meaning of a person's words, it can apply to other cases too. The next steps show this.

phrases.english: You might have said:
the reason of Rabbi Meir there
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of a baby less than a month old.

phrases.english: is that he decreed about one less than a month old
because of one who is a month old;
but here, where there is no reason to decree,
say that he would not obligate him.
It teaches us:
the reason of Rabbi Meir
is that a person does not say his words for nothing;

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא הָכָא וְלָא שְׁנָא הָכָא.
phrases.english: there is no difference between here and here.
phrases.notes: The two cases are the baby and the כלי.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's ruling shows that רבי מאיר's reason is not a גזירה but 'a person does not speak for nothing,' which applies to a כלי as well.

steps.title: Whose view is רב's ruling about consecrating a friend's animal?
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that one who consecrates a friend's animal must give its value. The גמרא says this follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? רבה בר יוסף said in רב's name, and some say רב ייבא בר יוסי said in רב's name: one who consecrates his friend's animal gives its value. Whose view? רבי מאיר's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling of רב and asks which תנא it follows. It answers right away: רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot consecrate an animal that is not his. Since a person does not speak for nothing, we read his words as a pledge to pay the animal's value. This uses the same principle we just learned from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom does it go?
One who consecrates (makes something הקדש)
His fellow's animal
Monetary value

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: that Rabba bar Yosef said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב יֵיבָא בַּר יוֹסֵי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Yeiva bar Yosei said that Rav said:
One who consecrates his friend's animal
gives its value?
In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי מאיר's principle from step 2 to a new ruling of רב
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view underlies רב's ruling about consecrating a friend's animal?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It follows רבי מאיר: a person does not speak for nothing, so he meant to pledge the animal's value.

steps.title: Didn't רב already say this idea once?
steps.stepSummary: רב already taught that 'ערך כלי עלי' obligates the value, so why say the same idea again about a friend's animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב already said this once, as רב גידל said in רב's name: one who says 'the ערך of a כלי is upon me' gives its value!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: why would רב repeat the same principle in two rulings?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rulings rest on the same idea: words that can't take effect as said are read as a pledge of value. If רב already taught this with the כלי, the ruling about the friend's animal seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: One time (already once)
The 'ערך' of a utensil, which has no ערך
Upon me (wording of a pledge)

phrases.english: But Rav already said it once,
as Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
One who says: 'The valuation of a utensil is upon me'
gives its value!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אַמְרַהּ רַב חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling cited in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling about consecrating a friend's animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems to repeat the principle רב already taught with ערך כלי, so it should be unnecessary.

steps.title: With a כלי, the person clearly meant money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer: in the כלי case, everyone knows a כלי has no ערך. So the person surely meant its value, and that may not be true in other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that only there does he pay, because he knows a כלי has no ערך. So he decided to give money, and he said 'ערך' meaning its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain why both rulings are needed. It shows what is special about the כלי case. The other half of the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody thinks a כלי has a ערך, so 'ערך כלי' can only mean money. An animal is different, because it really can become holy. So we might have read his words as an attempt to make the animal itself holy, and that would do nothing because it is not his. That is why the second ruling is needed, as the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: He knows
He decided in his mind and then said
Meaning the monetary value

steps.confusionAlert: This answer is not finished here. The גמרא has so far only explained the כלי side; the part explaining the friend's animal comes next.

phrases.english: You might have said that it is only there
phrases.notes: 'There' is the ערך כלי case.

phrases.english: since he knows that a utensil has no valuation,
and he decided and said it to mean its value.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא הָתָם הוּא דְּיוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֵין עֵרֶךְ לִכְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (both rulings are needed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the principle works only where the person clearly knows his words can't take effect as said, as with a כלי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Answer still in progress; it sets up why the friend's-animal ruling teaches something new.

steps.title: An animal can become holy, so we might think he meant the animal itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. An animal can be made holy, so we might think the person meant to make it holy right now and planned to buy it later. That would mean he never meant to pay its value, and his words would do nothing. רב teaches that he does have to pay its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: But an animal can be made holy. So one could say he meant this: 'If I ask its owner, he will sell it to me. Let it become holy from now, and I will offer it.' He was not talking about paying its value. So רב teaches us that he does pay its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started in step 5. It explains why the animal case is different from the כלי case, so רב needed to teach both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a כלי, there is no other way to read his words, so we know he meant its value. An animal is different, because it really can become holy. So we could have read his words as an attempt to make the animal itself holy, which fails because it is not his. רב's ruling tells us we still treat his words as a promise to pay its value.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that is fit to be made holy (an animal can be brought as a קרבן)
From now, starting right away
Its value, what it is worth in money
This teaches us (the new point the ruling adds)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's two rulings are both needed. A כלי can only mean its value. An animal could have meant making the animal itself holy, so we needed רב to tell us that the person still pays its value.

phrases.english: But an animal, which is something that can be made holy
one could say that this is what he means:
If I tell its owner
he will sell it to me,
so let it become holy from now, and I will offer it,
but he is not talking about its value,
so רב teaches us that he does pay its value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בְּהֵמָה, דְּבַת מִיקְדַּשׁ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 5 by giving the other side of the comparison: the animal case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a כלי cannot be made holy as an ערך, but an animal can be made holy as a קרבן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since an animal can become holy, we might think he meant to make the animal itself holy. That fails because it is not his, so he would owe nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב teaches that he means its value and must pay it. So the animal ruling adds something new beyond the כלי ruling.

steps.title: רב אשי: only when he says 'upon me'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי limits רב's ruling. The person owes the animal's value only if he said 'עלי' (it is upon me). If he said 'הרי זו' (this animal is holy), he owes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This is only when he said 'upon me.' But if he said 'this is [holy],' he does not owe anything.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי sets a limit on רב's ruling about a friend's animal. The exact words the person used make the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עלי' means he takes on a duty himself, so we can read it as a promise to pay the value. 'הרי זו' points at the animal itself and tries to make it holy. He cannot do that to an animal he does not own, so nothing happens.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Upon me': the person takes on a personal duty to give
'This is': the person declares that this very object is holy

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea in vows to the בית המקדש. 'עלי' creates a personal debt. 'הרי זו' acts on a specific object, and it works only if the object belongs to him.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And this is only when he said 'upon me,'
but if he said 'this one is holy,' he does not owe anything.
phrases.notes: 'This one' means his friend's animal, which he has no power to make holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וְהוּא דְּאָמַר עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to רב's ruling that was just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling applies only when the person said 'עלי'. If he said 'הרי זו' about his friend's animal, he owes nothing.

steps.title: New משנה: can a נכרי be valued or make an ערך vow?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי מאיר says a נכרי can be the one whose ערך is given, but he cannot make an ערך vow himself. רבי יהודה says the opposite. Both agree that a נכרי can make a vow to give a value and can be the subject of such a vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: A gentile: רבי מאיר says he can be valued, but he cannot make an ערך vow. רבי יהודה says he can make an ערך vow, but he cannot be valued. Both agree that he can make vows of value and can be the subject of vows of value.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: how a נכרי fits into the laws of ערכין. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two roles. One is the person who makes the vow (מעריך). The other is the person whose ערך is given (נערך). רבי מאיר lets a נכרי fill only the second role, and רבי יהודה lets him fill only the first. A vow to give someone's market value (נדר) works both ways according to both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: A gentile, someone who is not Jewish
Is valued: he is the one whose fixed ערך someone promises to give
Makes an ערך vow: he promises to give someone's fixed ערך
They make vows of value and are the subject of vows of value (market worth, not the fixed ערך)
Both of them agree

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ערך and נדר. An ערך is a fixed amount set by the תורה based on age and gender. A נדר of value ('דמי עלי') means what the person would sell for on the market. The מחלוקת here is only about ערך.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A gentile: Rabbi Meir says:
He can be valued, but he cannot make an ערך vow.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
He can make an ערך vow, but he cannot be valued.
And both of them agree
that they can make vows of value and be the subject of vows of value.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָכְרִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic, not connected to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a נכרי can be valued but cannot make an ערך vow. רבי יהודה: he can make an ערך vow but cannot be valued. Both agree on vows of value (נדרים).

steps.title: ברייתא: 'בני ישראל' make ערך vows, gentiles do not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא based on the פסוק 'דבר אל בני ישראל'. It teaches that Jews can make an ערך vow, but gentiles cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The children of Israel can make an ערך vow, and gentiles cannot make an ערך vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts looking for the sources behind the משנה's מחלוקת. It begins with a ברייתא that reads the words of the פסוק closely. This is the start of a longer ברייתא that continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערכין section of the תורה opens with 'speak to בני ישראל.' The ברייתא learns from this that the ability to make an ערך vow belongs to Jews, which fits רבי מאיר's view that a נכרי cannot make one. The ברייתא will go on to explain the rest of the מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: The children of Israel, the Jewish people (from the פסוק that opens ערכין)
Gentiles, the nations

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
The children of Israel can make an ערך vow
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:2

phrases.english: and gentiles cannot make an ערך vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַעֲרִיכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins finding the source in the פסוק for the rulings in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'בני ישראל' we learn that Jews can make an ערך vow and gentiles cannot.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the word 'איש' lets a נכרי be valuated
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A נכרי cannot make an ערך vow, but the word 'איש' teaches that his ערך can still be given. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a נכרי also cannot be valuated. So the פסוק says 'איש' (a man). These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes רבי מאיר's reading. 'בני ישראל' took away the נכרי's power to make the vow, and now 'איש' puts him back in as someone whose ערך can be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 used 'בני ישראל' to leave out gentiles as מעריכין. That might have suggested they are left out completely. The broad word 'איש' brings them back in, but only as נערכין.

keyTerms.meaning: The person whose ערך is being given (the subject of the vow)
'You might think', which sets up a wrong idea that the פסוק will correct
'The פסוק teaches', which introduces the word that settles the question
'A man', a broad word that includes even a נכרי

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two words apart. מעריך is the one who MAKES the vow ('I owe my ערך' or someone else's). נערך is the one whose ערך is being given. Most of this sugya depends on this difference.

phrases.english: You might think they [gentiles] cannot be valuated?
The verse teaches: 'a man,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:2

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהוּ נֶעֱרָכִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִישׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in Step 9 by adding the second פסוק word, 'איש'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a נכרי can be נערך because of the word 'איש', even though he cannot be מעריך.

steps.title: רבי מאיר asks why he split the פסוקים this way
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר asks himself: one word includes gentiles and one leaves them out, so why do I say they can be valuated but cannot make the vow, and not the other way around?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: Since one פסוק includes and one פסוק excludes, why do I say he can be valuated but cannot make the vow?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר raises a question about his own reading. This sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two words point in opposite directions. 'איש' includes gentiles and 'בני ישראל' leaves them out. Either word could be matched to either role, so he must explain why 'איש' goes with נערך and 'בני ישראל' goes with מעריך.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק (verse)
Includes, adds more cases
Excludes, leaves cases out
The one who makes the ערך vow

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
Since one verse includes
phrases.notes: That is 'איש'.

phrases.english: and one verse excludes,
phrases.notes: That is 'בני ישראל'.

phrases.english: for what reason do I say
he is valuated but does not make the vow?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֲנִי אוֹמֵר נֶעֱרָךְ וְלֹא מַעֲרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind the reading given in Steps 9 and 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why 'איש' is matched with נערך and 'בני ישראל' with מעריך, and not the reverse.

steps.title: The תורה includes more people as נערכין than as מעריכין
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that the תורה is wider about who can be valuated than about who can make the vow. A חרש, a שוטה and a קטן can be valuated but cannot make the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק includes more people among those who are valuated than among those who make the vow. A חרש, a שוטה and a קטן are valuated, but they cannot make the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers his own question. Since the תורה already gives the wider category to נערכין, the including word 'איש' belongs there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the group of נערכין is bigger, because people without full understanding can be valuated but cannot make a vow. So the extra including word should go to the bigger group, and the excluding word should go to the smaller group of מעריכין.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק included more people
A deaf-mute, who cannot make binding statements
A person without mental competence
A minor

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's rule: when one word includes and another excludes, give the including word to the category the תורה already treats more widely. That is why a נכרי is נערך but not מעריך.

phrases.english: Because the verse included more among those who are valuated
than among those who make the vow,
for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor are valuated,
phrases.notes: This comes from the very first משנה of the מסכת, on דף 2a.

phrases.english: but they do not make the vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרִיבָּה הַכָּתוּב בַּנֶּעֱרָכִין יוֹתֵר מִבַּמַּעֲרִיכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה already includes more people as נערכין (חרש, שוטה, קטן), so the including word 'איש' belongs to that category.

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads the פסוקים the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says 'בני ישראל' means only Jews can be valuated, and 'איש' means a נכרי can still make the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: בני ישראל are valuated, but gentiles are not valuated. You might think they also cannot make the vow? So the פסוק says 'איש'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי יהודה's view. He uses the same two words but swaps their roles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, 'בני ישראל' limits who can be valuated, and 'איש' includes gentiles as vow-makers. This matches his opinion in the משנה from Step 8: a נכרי is מעריך but not נערך.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The children of Israel', the word used to leave gentiles out
Gentiles (נכרים)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that both תנאים agree on which פסוק words matter. They argue only about which role each word controls.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
'The children of Israel' are valuated
but gentiles are not valuated;
you might think they cannot make the vow?
The verse teaches: 'a man.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶעֱרָכִין וְאֵין הַגּוֹיִם נֶעֱרָכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same פסוקים that רבי מאיר used in Steps 9 through 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a נכרי can be מעריך because of 'איש', but he cannot be נערך because of 'בני ישראל'.

steps.title: רבי יהודה asks himself why he rules his way
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה asks: one word includes gentiles and one leaves them out, so why do I say a נכרי can make the vow but cannot be valuated?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: Since one verse includes and one verse excludes, why do I say a gentile can make a valuation vow but cannot be valuated?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה asks himself the same kind of question רבי מאיר asked in Step 11. The גמרא is setting up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions use the same two words: 'איש' includes gentiles and 'בני ישראל' leaves them out. רבי יהודה must explain why he puts the 'include' on making the vow and the 'leave out' on being valuated. That is the opposite of what רבי מאיר does.

keyTerms.meaning: includes, widens the rule
excludes, narrows the rule
makes an ערך vow (pledges someone's value)
is valuated (his value can be pledged)
a verse or word of the תורה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Since one verse includes
phrases.notes: That is the word 'איש', which includes gentiles.

phrases.english: and one verse excludes,
phrases.notes: That is 'בני ישראל', which leaves gentiles out.

phrases.english: for what reason do I say
a gentile makes a valuation vow but is not valuated?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁמִּקְרָא אֶחָד מְרַבֶּה וּמִקְרָא אֶחָד מְמַעֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה now defends his own reading, just as רבי מאיר defended his.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי יהודה apply the inclusion to making the vow and the exclusion to being valuated?

steps.title: The תורה is wider about who can make the vow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that the תורה includes more people among those who make the vow than among those who are valuated. A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס can make the vow but cannot be valuated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the verse included more people among those who make valuation vows than among those who are valuated. A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס can make valuation vows but cannot be valuated.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives his answer. The group of people who can make the vow is bigger than the group of people who can be valuated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה has a clear example: a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס can make the vow but cannot be valuated. So it makes sense that a נכרי fits the same pattern. This is the exact opposite of רבי מאיר's answer in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse included (more people)
a person whose gender cannot be known because it is hidden
a person with both male and female features
for look, here is proof

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two answers. רבי מאיר says the תורה is wider about who can be VALUATED (Step 12). רבי יהודה says the תורה is wider about who can MAKE THE VOW (this step).

phrases.english: Because the verse included more among those who make valuation vows
than among those who are valuated,
for look, a tumtum and a hermaphrodite
phrases.notes: This rule comes from the first משנה of the מסכת.

phrases.english: make valuation vows but are not valuated.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרִיבָּה הַכָּתוּב בַּמַּעֲרִיכִין יוֹתֵר מִבַּנֶּעְרָכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רבי יהודה asked himself.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה includes more people as makers of the vow than as people who can be valuated, as we see with טומטום and אנדרוגינוס.

steps.title: רבא judges both opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי מאיר's ruling makes sense but his reason does not, and רבי יהודה's reason makes sense but his ruling does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי מאיר's ruling is reasonable, but his reason is not reasonable. רבי יהודה's reason is reasonable, but his ruling is not reasonable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a short summary verdict on both opinions. The גמרא is setting up the next steps, where רבא explains each part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא separates two things: the final ruling (הלכה) and the proof behind it (טעם). He says each תנא got one part right and one part wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: his ruling, his final law
his reason, his proof
makes sense, is reasonable

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches an important idea in learning: a ruling can be correct even when the proof given for it is weak, and the other way around.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Meir's ruling is reasonable,
his reason is not reasonable;
Rabbi Yehuda's reason is reasonable,
his ruling is not reasonable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הִלְכְתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both תנאים have explained themselves, an אמורא evaluates them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר's ruling is correct but his reason is weak. רבי יהודה's reason is strong but his ruling is wrong.

steps.title: Why רבי מאיר's ruling makes sense
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves רבי מאיר's ruling (a נכרי cannot make the vow) from the פסוק in עזרא: 'You have nothing to do with us to build a house to our God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר's ruling is reasonable, as it is written: 'You have nothing to do with us to build a house to our God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the first part of his verdict. A פסוק shows that gentiles have no share in building the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money from ערך vows goes to the upkeep of the בית המקדש. The Jews told the outsiders they could not help build it. So a נכרי's vow should not count, which is רבי מאיר's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: not for you, you have no part
and with us
as it is written

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir's ruling is reasonable,
as it is written: 'You have nothing to do with us
phrases.notes: עזרא ד:ג. The Jews returning from בבל said this to outsiders who wanted to help build.

phrases.english: to build a house to our God,'

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכְתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first part of רבא's verdict.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's ruling that a נכרי cannot make an ערך vow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עזרא ד:ג, 'לא לכם ולנו לבנות את בית אלהינו'.

steps.title: Why רבי מאיר's proof is weak
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's proof from חרש, שוטה and קטן does not work, because those people lack understanding. A נכרי does have understanding.
steps.simpleTranslation: His reason is not reasonable, because he brings it from a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן. But a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן are different, since they lack understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רבי מאיר's proof from Step 12. The comparison does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש, a שוטה and a קטן cannot make the vow because they lack the mental ability to commit. A נכרי has full understanding. So their case tells us nothing about a נכרי.

keyTerms.meaning: he brings it (as a proof)
is different
a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
people with understanding, mentally competent

phrases.english: His reason is not reasonable,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ מֵחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן,
phrases.english: since he brings it from a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor,
phrases.notes: This is the proof רבי מאיר gave back in Step 12.

phrases.english: a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor are different,
since they are not people with understanding.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמֵיהּ לָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ מֵחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second part of רבא's verdict about רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבי מאיר's proof is rejected. His ruling stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חרש, שוטה and קטן are left out because they lack understanding, which does not apply to a נכרי.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה's proof is strong
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's proof from טומטום and אנדרוגינוס works. They have full understanding and the תורה still leaves them out from being valuated, so they are a good comparison to a נכרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה's reason is reasonable, since he brings it from a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. Even though they are people with understanding, the Merciful One excluded them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why רבי יהודה's proof from Step 15 is a good one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס have full understanding, just like a נכרי. Even so, the תורה says they cannot be valuated. So the comparison to a נכרי fits well.

keyTerms.meaning: even though
excluded them
the Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda's reason is reasonable,
since he brings it from a tumtum and a hermaphrodite,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דִּבְנֵי דֵעָה נִינְהוּ
phrases.english: for even though they are people with understanding,
the Merciful One excluded them.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ מִטּוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite of Step 18: this proof works because the people in it do have understanding.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's reasoning that the group who can make the vow is wider than the group who can be valuated.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of טומטום and אנדרוגינוס, who have understanding yet cannot be valuated.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה's ruling does not hold
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's ruling, that a נכרי can make the vow, goes against the פסוק 'You have nothing to do with us to build a house to our God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: His ruling is not reasonable, as it is written: 'You have nothing to do with us to build a house to our God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his verdict. He uses the same פסוק from עזרא to reject רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that supports רבי מאיר in Step 17 works against רבי יהודה. Gentiles have no share in building the בית המקדש, so a נכרי's ערך vow should not count.

keyTerms.meaning: to build
the house of our God, the בית המקדש
does not make sense

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's verdict: רבי מאיר's ruling makes sense (a נכרי cannot make an ערך vow, based on עזרא ד:ג). But his proof from חרש, שוטה and קטן is weak, because they lack understanding. רבי יהודה's proof from טומטום and אנדרוגינוס is a good comparison, since they do have understanding, but his ruling goes against the פסוק.

phrases.english: His ruling is not reasonable,
as it is written: 'You have nothing to do with us
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as in Step 17, עזרא ד:ג.

phrases.english: to build a house to our God.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכְתֵיהּ לָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's verdict about רבי יהודה by rejecting his ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבי יהודה's ruling is rejected. His proof stays strong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His ruling lets gentiles share in the בית המקדש through ערך vows, which goes against עזרא ד:ג.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In רבא's judgment, רבי מאיר's ruling (a נכרי cannot make an ערך vow) is the more reasonable one, and טומטום and אנדרוגינוס are the better proof. The גמרא then asks how רבי יהודה deals with the פסוק, and steps 21 to 24 answer.

steps.title: How does רבי יהודה explain the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה does with the פסוק 'You have nothing to do with us.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, what does he do with this פסוק, 'You have nothing to do with us'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה explains the פסוק from עזרא that seems to go against him. This sets up the next step, which gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 רבא said this פסוק shows a נכרי cannot give to the בית המקדש. רבי יהודה says a נכרי can make an ערכין vow. So he must read this פסוק some other way, and the גמרא wants to know how.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Not for you and us', meaning 'You have nothing to do with us' (עזרא 4:3)
What does he do with it? (How does he explain this source?)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda,
this verse 'You have nothing to do with us'
phrases.notes: עזרא 4:3

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַאי ״לָא לָכֶם וְלָנוּ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 20 used the פסוק against רבי יהודה's ruling. Now the גמרא asks how רבי יהודה himself would read that פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבי יהודה understand the פסוק 'You have nothing to do with us', given that he lets a נכרי make an ערכין vow?

steps.title: The valuation money is put away
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting אבימי, says the פסוק teaches that a נכרי's ערך money is put away and not used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: his ערך money is put away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as being about what happens to the money. The vow is valid, but the money is hidden away and not used for the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer lets רבי יהודה keep his ruling that a נכרי's vow takes effect. The words 'nothing to do with us' are read as being only about using the money. The money is not used for building the בית המקדש, so it is put away.

keyTerms.meaning: His valuation: the fixed amount owed for a person's ערך
Is put away (hidden and never used)

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said that Avimi said:
And his valuation money is put away.
phrases.notes: Put away means it is set aside and never used for the בית המקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר אֲבִימִי: וְעֶרְכּוֹ נִגְנָז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק does not cancel the vow. It only teaches that the money from a נכרי's ערך is put away instead of being used for the בית המקדש.

steps.title: If the money is put away, why is there misuse?
steps.stepSummary: If a נכרי's ערך money is put away, there should be no מעילה on it. But a ברייתא says a נכרי's gifts for בדק הבית do carry מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, there should be no מעילה on it. We learned that for the five sin offerings left to die, and for money thrown into the Dead Sea, one may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה. So why does a ברייתא say about non-Jews' consecrated items: when is this said? For items given to the altar. But for items given to בדק הבית, there is מעילה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's answer. Things that are put away and never used carry no מעילה. Yet a ברייתא says a נכרי's gifts for בדק הבית do carry מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that things the בית המקדש will never use, like the five sin offerings left to die or money thrown into the Dead Sea, carry no מעילה. If a נכרי's ערך money were put away, it would be just like them, with no מעילה. But the ברייתא says a נכרי's בדק הבית gifts do carry מעילה, which shows they are really used. So 'put away' cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: the way the גמרא shows that an answer leads to a bad result
Misusing holy property for personal benefit. Doing it by mistake requires an offering.
The five sin offerings that cannot be brought and are left to die
The Dead Sea, where useless holy money is thrown
Items given for the altar (offerings)
Items given for the upkeep of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'may not benefit' with 'is liable for מעילה.' The five sin offerings and the Dead Sea money are still forbidden to use. But using them does not count as מעילה, because the בית המקדש never gets any use from them.

phrases.english: But if that is so,
one should not be liable for misusing it,
as we learned:
the five sin offerings that are left to die,
and money that goes to the Dead Sea:
one may not benefit from them, but there is no liability for misuse!
Why, then, is it taught about the consecrated items of non-Jews:
When is this said?
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule that non-Jews' consecrated items carry no מעילה. The ברייתא is limiting it.

phrases.english: With items consecrated for the altar.
But with items consecrated for the upkeep of the Temple,
one is liable for misusing them?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, לֹא יִמְעֲלוּ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim, quoting אבימי, that a נכרי's ערך money is put away.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Things that are put away carry no מעילה, like the five sin offerings and the Dead Sea money. But a ברייתא says a נכרי's בדק הבית gifts carry מעילה. That shows they are used, not put away.

steps.title: The refusal was to stop discouragement
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the refusal in עזרא was not a halachic rule. It happened because those non-Jews were trying to weaken the builders.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: it was because of weakening the hands, as it is written: 'Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah and frightened them from building.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new explanation of the פסוק for רבי יהודה. The Jews turned those non-Jews away because they were trying to discourage the builders, not because of any halachic rule about gifts from a נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's answer fell apart, so רבא says the פסוק teaches no halacha at all. It describes a practical response to people who were working against the building. This means a נכרי's ערך money can go to בדק הבית and carry מעילה, just as the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: Weakening of the hands: discouraging people so they lose the will to act
Here: the local non-Jewish population (not the usual meaning of an unlearned Jew)
Frightening or harassing

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי יהודה reads 'You have nothing to do with us' as a one-time practical move against people trying to stop the building. It is not a rule that a נכרי's gifts are refused. So a נכרי's ערך money goes to בדק הבית.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא may read a story in תנ״ך as a response to its own time rather than a lasting halacha. That reading is what lets רבי יהודה keep his ruling.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It was because of the weakening of hands,
phrases.notes: He means the Jews refused those non-Jews because they were trying to discourage the builders.

phrases.english: as it is written:
'Then the people of the land
weakened the hands of the people of Judah
and frightened them from building.'
phrases.notes: עזרא 4:4

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: מִשּׁוּם רִפְיוֹן יָדַיִם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 23 knocked down רב חסדא's answer. רבא replaces it with a different way to read the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the פסוק: it describes a historical situation, not a halacha.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק was thought to set a halacha about a נכרי's gifts, either cancelling them or making them be put away.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק records a refusal made because those non-Jews were discouraging the builders. A נכרי's ערך money really goes to בדק הבית and carries מעילה.
